awd_titl_txt: Travel: SCH: NSF Student Travel Grant for the 2025 IEEE-EMBS International Conference on Body Sensor Networks (IEEE BSN)
awd_abstract_narration:
This project is to support student travel at the 2025 IEEE-EMBS International Conference on Body Sensor Networks (BSN 2025). BSN is the premier conference in the areas of sensors and systems for digital health. It will bring together leaders and experts in academia, industry, healthcare, and non-profit organizations to provide a cross-disciplinary, highly selective, and single-track forum for cutting-edge research related to devices and sensors, hardware and software systems, predictive models, and data analytics in the healthcare/medical domains. Student participants will have opportunities to receive professional support and career advice from internationally recognized experts. Travel support increases engagement with the research community and provides professionally significant opportunities to students who might otherwise not be able to attend the conference.

This project aims to increase the accessibility of the scientific forum that is BSN 2025. By attending BSN 2025, students may explore their interests, interact and network with seasoned professionals, and identify the various career paths available within the broader community of health scientists and technologists. With this registration award offsetting the cost of attendance, students who would otherwise find attendance expenses prohibitive can obtain these benefits. BSN 2025 will focus on cutting-edge innovations in computational medicine, including applications of novel sensors and artificial intelligence. Increasing student engagement through the reduction of expenses, this award constitutes an investment in the future of the medical sensor research community; a community that is critical to the next generation of healthcare.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
This award provided support for students to attend the 2025 IEEE International Conference on Body Sensor Networks (BSN), the premier conference on sensing systems for digital health. The theme of the conference was "Computational Medicine: Expanding Health through Sensing and AI." A total of 25 students selected from a pool of 67 applicants were supported by this award. Awardees were chosen by a three-member committee using a competitive selection process that assessed each applicant's potential to benefit from the award and attendance at the conference. Awardees included 17 doctoral students, four masters students, three undergraduate students, and one high school student working with local university faculty. Of the 25 awardees, 22 were first authors presenting their scientific contributions. The award was used to provide free registration to awardees, lowering the overall barrier of attendance. Beyond the usual benefits of attending the conference, awardees were invited to an additional networking session with academic and industry leaders in the field. Awardees whose scientific contributions were not chosen for full-length oral presentations received an opportunity to orally present their work in a student-focused rapid-fire session. All awardees completed reports detailing their activities during the conference, with many reports highlighting new connections and collaborators.

Intellectual Merit: A total of 25 students were able to attend the conference because of this award. These students broadened the audience for research presented at BSN and raised the level of interaction. Most awardees were first-time attendees of the conference, increasing the number of new connections and facilitating the introduction of these students into a broader scientific community. These students were able to learn from directly experts and the presentation of cutting-edge work. The additional networking and rapid-fire sessions for awardees served to increase the positive impact of attendance.

Broader Impacts: By enabling students to attend the conference, research presented at the conference was disseminated to a larger audience. Student education was supported both by the opportunity to present their work and through observation of high-quality research, talks, and panels. Networking opportunities provided to students increased their integration into the scientific community and created the potential for new collaborations. The inclusion of undergraduate and high school students served to increase their interest in scientific career paths, promoting the development of the national scientific workforce.
